qualification: Indicative uncontrolled-host experiments; pilots use 2s warmup + 3s measurement and two reversed-order repeats on Java 21. Longer plaintext controls use 3s + 5s on Java 21/25. All production candidates discarded.

experiments.name: tls-vectors
experiments.hypothesis: Reuse one-element SSLEngine wrap/unwrap vectors to reduce per-record allocation
experiments.decision: Discard: TLS +0.4%, H2 -0.7%; no CPU benefit.

experiments.name: tls-direct-output
experiments.hypothesis: Direct ciphertext output avoids the channel heap-to-native staging copy
experiments.decision: Discard: direct ciphertext output reduced TLS throughput 29.3% and H2 throughput 18.5%; correctness passed.

experiments.name: drain-lock
experiments.hypothesis: Avoid separately locking output to inspect pending bytes immediately before drainTo does the same check
experiments.decision: Discard: throughput and CPU were effectively flat, with a small-window p99 regression in the pilot.

experiments.name: selector-wake
experiments.hypothesis: Wake selector only while the owner may be selecting, with a queue recheck to avoid lost notifications
experiments.decision: Discard: fewer write-family calls did not improve throughput; TLS throughput -4.2% and CPU +7.1%.

experiments.name: owners
experiments.hypothesis: Eight rather than four transport owners improves TLS throughput enough to justify additional threads and buffers
experiments.decision: Keep existing default: eight owners improved H1 throughput but increased CPU 20–27% and reduced H2 throughput 8.8%; retain as configuration evidence only.

experiments.name: h2-batch
experiments.hypothesis: A 16KiB instead of 8KiB ready-frame batching threshold reduces transport handoffs

experiments.name: h2-credit
experiments.hypothesis: Mutable stream-credit cells avoid boxing and replacing map values on every DATA frame
experiments.decision: Discard: normal-window throughput +1.3% and small-window +0.6%; short-run CPU improvements near 1% do not establish a worthwhile benefit for the added mutable credit state.

experiments.name: plain-quantum
experiments.hypothesis: Double plaintext service quantum/socket write limit to 262432 bytes; preserve TLS limits and owned buffers; inspect native-buffer and fairness costs
experiments.decision: Discard: longer bulk throughput +3.9%/+5.1% on Java 21/25, but repeated active-writer shared-owner p99 regressed 36.5%/43.2%; about 0.5 MiB more Java 21 buffer-pool storage with four owners.
